# 3.2.x Vulcanus discovery recovery preparation

This disposable three-stage fixture keeps the single `mir-fixture-discovery-recovery` identity while a published MIR 3.2.0 or 3.2.1 source save is handed to MIR5 on official Factorio 2.1.23 Space Age. The source validates the emitted historical iron row, including its exact unordered `iron-plate` and `casting-iron` productivity vector. For 3.2.0 it requires the one retained `planet-discovery-vulcanus` travel effect and observes a researched discovery with Vulcanus naturally locked after the actual source lab. For 3.2.1 it requires the official ordered `unlock-space-location` Vulcanus and travel effects and observes the naturally unlocked result after that lab. It retains the source iron formula `8000*2^(L-1)` and time `60`, accelerating only the source discovery lab. The MIR5 successor verifies that same iron unit without changing it, then verifies the unqueued `recipe-prod-research_gears-1` Space Age row: its ordered `casting-iron-gear-wheel` and `iron-gear-wheel` productivity effects are each `.1`, its four science packs are each one, and its formula/time are the same. Only that gear row is accelerated to one count and five seconds. It records the actual initial gear level and `iron-gear-wheel` bonus, then requires exactly one level and one native `.1` effect increment. It does not insert an unlock effect or call `lock_space_location` to manufacture either source state. The scripted iron level-three/42-percent queue witness is fixture state, not a published default or an observation of the historical defect.

The source also creates a separate foreign force with unresearched locked Vulcanus and a 27-percent iron queue. Before it creates a laboratory or writes successor storage, the MIR5 successor preserves the protected source state and foreign lock, both iron queues, the player level-three 20-percent iron-plate contribution, saved-progress domain/value, and the protected same-mod fixture state. Only after that strict initial match does the fixture pause its own single-element player iron queue with the documented complete `research_queue` write, run the one gear lab, restore the captured ordered iron TechnologyID queue and `.42` progress, and read it back. It never uses `cancel_current_research()`. A queue refusal reports only the already-read expected/actual IDs, lengths, progress, and Vulcanus flag before the unchanged strict comparison; a restoration readback refusal is a fixture-operation failure rather than product preflight evidence. The 3.2.0 successor route additionally requires ordinary MIR recovery to restore its researched player location; the fresh 3.2.1 route is a no-repair retention control and cannot show that a 3.2.0-to-3.2.1 handoff repaired an inherited lock. It then proves supplied science was consumed by one current gear laboratory, saves, and requires two read-only cold reload observations while preserving the restored player `.42` and foreign `.27` work.

The 3.2.0 wrapper deliberately refuses if its actual emitted `planet-discovery-vulcanus` row is absent or has the wrong retained effect. Historical evidence records that a 3.2.0 external discovery target could be pruned; this fixture never recreates, unhides, or substitutes that prototype to force an input through. The 3.2.1 wrapper likewise refuses a missing or wrong Vulcanus unlock effect. Black Glass reports the frozen 3.2.0 source under original controller11999752/raw c17 and protected saveEC0E as passed; its original native inputs remain authoritative. The 3.2.1 source remains prepared and unqualified. Neither result becomes an R05 successor pass.

Each stage is a five-member caller-composed fixture projection: the stage `info.json`, `control.lua`, and `data-final-fixes.lua`, plus the shared `fixture_control.lua` and `fixture_data_final.lua`. The [R04 prepared-input record](../../../spec/evidence/discovery-recovery-prepared-inputs-r04.json) remains the earlier prepared comparison. The [R05 successor-only baseline packet](../../../spec/evidence/discovery-recovery-prepared-inputs-r05.json) binds the native-owner-reported frozen 3.2.0 source save and the a575 candidate; this fixture does not recreate that source or select the proposed helper. Its separate a575 control observes whether the engine itself restores discovery; a control pass cannot establish that the helper ran or was necessary. The original source hashes are bound by the R05 packet. The [separate R05 native chain](../../../spec/evidence/discovery-recovery-a575-native-chain-r05.json) records the exact a575/7CE successor lab, save and two cold reloads under their original identities; Black Glass retains native scheduling and exclusive library ownership. This preparation does not qualify a full 3.2 catalogue, ordinary science tuning, historical bug cause, performance, Library behavior, multiplayer, or release readiness.

The [current005D prepared inputs](../../../spec/evidence/discovery-recovery-current005d-prepared-inputs-r01.json) and [separate selection](../../profiles/discovery-recovery-successor-current005d-r05-f210-2123.json) reuse protectedEC0E with the same five-member A7E successor and two-member2E1 observer. Supply both source directories through `FixtureSources`; the existing runner requires the named observer to be independently verified alongside the successor. The prepared packet passes those host guards, including rejection of its original missing-observer draft, but still needs an actual current005D native lab/save/two-reload result. Preserve the queued iron unit and all source-state/foreign-lock checks; this preparation neither selects a proposed automatic helper nor extends the claim to3.2.1 or ambiguous later locks.
